title: US proposes fresh tariffs of up to 35% on 14 economies
summary:
The US has proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies over structural manufacturing overcapacity, with Vietnam facing up to 35 per cent, India 25 per cent, and China and Singapore 20 per cent each. 
Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia face up to 18 per cent. 
India's rate could be reduced to 17 per cent under a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the investigation’s findings.

title: Denmark's $550 mn investment to lift Bangladesh's port capacity by 44%
summary:
Bangladesh's proposed Laldia Container Terminal in Chattogram, backed by a $550 million investment from Denmark's APM Terminals, is expected to increase port capacity by 44 per cent. 
Part of the EU's Global Gateway initiative, the project will improve port efficiency, accommodate larger vessels and strengthen trade connectivity. 
It is scheduled to become operational in 2030.

title: China’s central bank to drain net $29.9 bn via lending facility
summary:
China's central bank will conduct an 800-billion-yuan  (~$119.8 billion) one-year MLF operation on Wednesday to maintain ample liquidity in the banking system. 
The fixed-quantity, interest-rate bidding process will result in a net withdrawal of 200 billion yuan (~$29.9 billion) as 1 trillion yuan matures this month. 
The PBOC also plans a 500-billion-yuan (~$74.9 billion) seven-day reverse repo operation.

title: 24% higher in US dollars: Can wool buyers absorb the cost rise?
summary:
Australia’s benchmark wool price rose for a second consecutive sale, with the AWEX EMI at 1,738 A¢/kg clean on November 18.
The index was about 15 per cent above the same week in 2025 but 8.7 per cent below its 2026/27 season-opening level after a November 4 low.
TexPro and ABARES data signal higher annual costs for topmakers, spinners, mills and autumn/winter 2027 sourcing.

title: US tariff probe: Can India strengthen its apparel export advantage?
summary:
US Section 301 duties are being prepared for India and 15 other economies over alleged structural excess capacity, putting textiles and apparel exports under scrutiny.
The US Trade Representative had issued no findings, rates or product lists by November 25; India already faces a 10 per cent extra duty since July 24.
Final rates could affect sourcing versus Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Record US imports: Real demand or early orders ahead of tariffs
summary:
US container imports hit 2.67 million TEUs in October; apparel imports reached $59.7 billion and footwear $21.2 billion in January-September.
China-origin goods held 29.9-36.3 per cent of US container imports in January-September, while China and Vietnam led apparel sourcing.
Tariff risks, Middle East conflict and Red Sea security concerns make year-end volumes hard to predict.

title: Durst to showcase digital textile printing at India ITME 2026
summary:
Durst Group will showcase its Alpha 330 dual-roll printer and LF direct-to-fabric series at India ITME 2026 with Fortuna Colours & Prints.
Following Aleph’s integration and a €20 million (~$21.93 million) Como hub investment, it aims to expand digital printing for fashion and home textiles.
Visit the Italian Pavilion, Hall 10, Booth G19, on 4–9 December.

title: India’s man-made yarn prices ease, wedding season offers hope
summary:
India’s man-made yarn market stayed bearish as weak demand, tight payments and cheaper raw materials cut polyester, polyester-cotton and viscose prices.
Polyester and blended yarn fell ₹2-4 (~$0.02–0.04) per kg in Ludhiana and Surat; viscose eased ₹2-4 in Surat and Mumbai on cheaper imports.
North Indian cotton dropped ₹20 per maund on weak ICE cues and slow mill demand; wedding-season demand may help.

title: 165,000 tonnes of TPA capacity exit: Can Japan secure new supplies?
summary:
Japan is set to rely fully on imported purified terephthalic acid (TPA) as Toray Industries plans to end domestic output by March 2027.
METI puts remaining capacity at about 165,000 tonnes, while 2025 imports from Thailand, South Korea and Indonesia reached about 232,000 tonnes.
MOF has proposed removing the 5.3 per cent duty from April 2027, potentially widening supply from Taiwan and Turkiye.

title: BTMA, ITTA webinar series to boost UK-India textile collaboration
summary:
BTMA and ITTA will conduct a technical webinar series to help Indian manufacturers improve quality, reduce waste and explore advanced textile technologies.
Sessions will cover coating and laminating, functional fabric testing, fibre handling, impregnation, automated inspection and yarn bonding.
The webinar series will be facilitated by the UKITMC, an initiative of BTMA, supported by the UK Government.

title: AAFA backs new US law to improve counterfeit detection & enforcement
summary:
AAFA has welcomed President Trump’s signing of the Customs Notification Act (H.R. 4930), saying it adds protection against illicit and dangerous goods ahead of peak holiday shopping. 
The law clarifies CBP information-sharing with brands during IP enforcement at the border, including data from products, packaging and packing materials. 
AAFA says it also expands who may receive CBP information.

title: Bangladesh's wage board proposes 36% hike to $136 for garment workers
summary:
Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board has proposed a 36 per cent increase in the monthly minimum wage for garment workers to Tk17,000 ($136) from Tk12,500, following negotiations and a vote. 
The proposal awaits labour ministry approval, with implementation expected from December 2026. 
The decision follows weeks of worker protests demanding higher wages amid rising living costs.

title: US’ Nike extends Michigan State University partnership through 2035
summary:
Nike and Michigan State University have extended their all-sports partnership for eight years, carrying a 26-year relationship through June 30, 2035.
The deal includes custom basketball and football alternate uniforms, Michigan State-specific basketball footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab access for student-athletes and preferred Nike testing-partner recognition.

title: €58 mn denim shift raises stakes for Egypt, China and Bangladesh
summary:
Bangladesh remains the European Union's top denim supplier, but imports from the country fell 5.48 per cent to $1.10 billion in January to September 2026.
Egypt gained $63.6 million, almost matching Bangladesh's $63.4 million loss, while China rose 20.23 per cent and Turkey lost $137.7 million.
TexPro trouser data and Egypt's garment network point to a 2027 contest over finishing and speed.

title: UK's Coats targets 2026 EBIT margin near 20% as profits stay resilient
summary:
UK's Coats expects full-year organic revenue to be broadly flat and earnings before interest and tax margin at or above 20 per cent, while strong free cash flow is set to reduce year-end leverage to around 2.0 times.
Revenue was flat organically in the four months to October 31, as apparel grew 3 per cent and footwear fell 7 per cent amid more pronounced destocking by brands.

title: Labour groups put living wage for Bangladesh garment workers at $265
summary:
Nine international labour rights organisations have urged Bangladesh’s RMG Minimum Wage Board to set wages in line with living costs during the ongoing review. 
They cited a living-wage estimate of about Tk 33,000 (~$265), alongside worker proposals of Tk 32,000 for skilled workers and Tk 30,000 for trainees. 
The groups also asked buyers to absorb increases and avoid shifting orders.

title: South Korea's Misto Holdings mentors future textile, fashion talent
summary:
South Korea's Misto Holdings participated in the 2026 Mentoring Academic Camp, offering textile and fashion students industry exposure.
Around 20 participants visited its headquarters for business presentations, workplace tours and career mentoring.
Students also toured KOTITI Testing & Research Institute to gain insights into textile quality, testing and research, supporting industry talent.

title: 341 factories shut amid Bangladesh’s $13.75 bn garment rebound
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel rebound faces 341 factory closures ahead of wage talks, with disruption losses estimated at Tk30–40 billion (~$241–322 million).
July–October exports rose 5.82 per cent to $13.75 billion, but EU and US import data signal weaker demand.
TexPro flags buyer-market concentration and reliance on Chinese and Indian inputs.

title: Bangladesh's garment sector loses $682 mn amid labour unrest: BGMEA
summary:
Bangladesh's garment sector has suffered losses of around $682 million across 317 factories due to labour unrest, production disruptions and relocated export orders, according to BGMEA. 
The losses include $428 million in disrupted production and $254 million in orders shifted to other countries over November 1-18, the association said.

title: US-China truce: Garment exports up 19.7%; will port fees raise costs?
summary:
US-China trade truce expires on January 10, 2027 with no tariff changes announced, leaving main US duties on Chinese garments outside the truce.
Chinese cotton knit T-shirts carry a combined 36.5 per cent US duty, against 29 per cent for Vietnam and 26.5 per cent for Bangladesh and India.
US port-fee suspensions and 178 Section 301 exclusions end on January 9 unless extended.
